title: Rubrik Carries an AI Premium While Its Own Forecast Signals Deceleration
subtitle: Wall Street bought the corporate undo button as an agentic play, but the math still looks like enterprise backup.
summary: Rubrik surged this autumn after rolling out governance tools for autonomous agents before tumbling alongside the broader software complex. The company must now prove in its December print that its growth justifies a rich multiple despite an implied second-half slowdown.

bodyHtml:
Think of Rubrik as the enterprise equivalent of an untouchable undo button. When you delete a photo on your phone, you pull it back from the cloud without sweating. For a hospital or an airline hit by ransomware, recovery is rarely that simple. Hackers spend weeks quietly lurking inside corporate networks, corrupting secondary drives and deleting logs before dropping a ransom note. When the alarm sounds, the backups companies thought they had are already poisoned.

Rubrik solves that problem by selling software that keeps an isolated, immutable record of every corporate file. Production credentials cannot touch its vaults, meaning an attacker who steals your network passwords still cannot wipe the clean copy. It maps out a data graph—indexing what exists, who touched it, and what dependencies need to fire up first. Large enterprises and government agencies pay hefty subscriptions for this insurance because it turns weeks of forensic chaos into an orderly restoration.

Lately, that safety net has taken on a new role: serving as the black box for generative AI. If an enterprise runs thousands of autonomous software agents to write code or query customer data, someone has to track what those bots touch. Rubrik rolled out tools like Agent Rewind and Agent Identity to reverse whatever rogue bots break and police what tools they reach. If Nvidia builds the high-speed engine, Rubrik wants to be the emergency brake.

Wall Street loved the pitch. Investors spent six weeks treating Rubrik like a runaway AI darling, running the stock up roughly 61% from its September lows. Then the broader tech trade cracked in early November after a Democratic midterm sweep sparked fears of a slower data-center buildout. Rubrik tumbled 11% in a single session, roughly twice the Nasdaq's slide, and now sits about a quarter below its peak.

Yet fundamentally, nothing inside the company shifted. Analyst ratings held, and the product cadence kept rolling. The market simply rethought what multiple it wanted to pay for the story.

That repricing brings an uncomfortable arithmetic problem to the surface. In the first half of its fiscal year, Rubrik posted revenue of $814 million, up over 38%. But parse the midpoint of management's full-year outlook, and second-half sales imply growth of just 20%, slowing toward 18% by the fourth quarter. It is tough to justify nearly 13 times guided sales and more than 70 times trailing free cash flow. The growth trajectory now looks less like an AI platform and more like a maturing IT utility.

That valuation gap is where the bears plant their flag. A short seller looking at this tape sees a business whose non-GAAP operating profit of $33.5 million exists only because it added back $101 million in quarterly stock-based compensation. Over the trailing twelve months, GAAP operating losses sit at $282 million. Worse, direct competitor Commvault trades at roughly 5.2 times sales while putting up a 21% operating margin and growing its subscription base at 20%.

Rubrik grows faster, but its cloud recurring revenue expansion cooled from 57% a year ago to 39% in the latest quarter, and net retention drifted down to just over 119%. When Dell gives away backup appliances inside hardware refreshes and hyperscalers offer basic storage for pennies, terminal margins face a low ceiling. The proof point arrives with the fiscal third-quarter print expected in early December. If subscription annual recurring revenue fails to track toward the roughly $1.88 billion pace the full-year outlook requires, the growth story breaks.

For the equity to re-rate from here, management must prove this second-half slowdown is routine conservatism rather than the start of a structural slide. The company has beaten forecasts three quarters running, backed by $1.75 billion in cash and zero-coupon debt that costs nothing to service. What we are watching in the December report is whether net recurring revenue can top the $91 million added last quarter. We also want to see whether those agentic tools convert into subscription cash or stay on press releases.

Rubrik built a genuine technical moat by securing the data companies cannot afford to lose. Now it has to convince public markets that it is an indispensable growth asset, not just an expensive way to buy peace of mind.

Disclosure: The Signal holds no position in RBRK. Positions may change. This is not financial advice.
